fatal_errors: The proposed CALPHAD screening method does not reconstruct the target HEBM-plus-SPS processing route.
The material system is changed from equimolar Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti powders to Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti compositions.

Computational prediction of equilibrium phase fractions and melting temperatures is presented as addressing microstructure refinement and property optimization without evidence of grain refinement, densification, hardness, or strength.
The falsification experiment compares efficiency with trial-and-error rather than validating predicted phases, microstructure, and mechanical properties experimentally.
explanation: The hypothesis is a literature-supported alternative for composition and phase-stability screening, but it has little agreement with the hidden target. The target uses high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering to create a dense nanocrystalline CoCrFeNiTi alloy with an 83% FCC/17% BCC structure and enhanced hardness and compressive strength. None of the target processing conditions, strengthening mechanisms, or quantitative outcomes are recovered. E1 supports screening Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti compositions for calculated phase fractions and melting temperatures, but it does not establish actual microstructure refinement or optimized mechanical properties. The stated database and composition limits are useful boundaries, although the proposed test is too indirect to discriminate whether the predicted candidates achieve the desired physical performance.
